title: Homogeneous coefficient criterion for a weakly regular module sequence
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $N$ an $R$-module, $s\geq0$, and $y_1,\ldots,y_s\in R$. Put $J=(y_1,\ldots,y_s)$. Suppose that for each $1\leq i\leq s$, multiplication by $y_i$ is injective on $N/(y_1,\ldots,y_{i-1})N$; this is condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], without any nonvanishing requirement. For $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s)\in\mathbb N^s$ write $|\alpha|=\sum_i\alpha_i$ and $y^\alpha=\prod_i y_i^{\alpha_i}$. Then for every $n\geq0$ and every family $(n_\alpha)_{|\alpha|=n}$ in $N$, one has
$$\sum_{|\alpha|=n}y^\alpha n_\alpha\in J^{n+1}N\quad\Longrightarrow\quad n_\alpha\in JN\ \text{for every }\alpha\text{ with }|\alpha|=n.$$
The module $N$ may be zero, and the parameter list may be empty. For $s=0$, the empty multi-index has degree zero and its monomial is $1$.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), part (2), and its proof, with equation-quasi-regular (Tag 061N). The module coefficient criterion is expanded explicitly. The proof uses only injectivity on successive quotients, so its argument also covers weak regularity and the zero module; it never uses the nonvanishing clause of regularity.

proof.text: For an ideal $H$, write $HN$ for the submodule of finite sums $\sum_j h_jv_j$ with $h_j\in H$ and $v_j\in N$. If $H=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$, expanding its generators gives $HN=\sum_i z_iN$. By the definition of ideal products and distributivity, $H^dN=\sum_{|\beta|=d}z^\beta N$: expand each product of $d$ generators, absorb all scalar coefficients into elements of $N$, and collect equal multi-indices; conversely every summand lies in $H^dN$. For $d=0$ the right side is $N$. In particular every $v\in H^{d+1}N=H^d(HN)$ has an expansion $v=\sum_{|\beta|=d}z^\beta b_\beta$ with $b_\beta\in HN$. These are finite sums, including when the list is empty.

source.place: Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular, proof of (1) and the module extension (2); Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular.

proof.text: Prove the asserted next-power coefficient criterion by induction on the length $s$, simultaneously for every degree $n$ and every weakly regular list of that length on $N$. At $s=0$ the ideal is zero: for $n=0$ the premise says that the single coefficient belongs to $0^1N=0$, and for $n>0$ there are no multi-indices. Thus the conclusion holds. Assume now that it holds in every degree for lists of length $s-1$, where $s\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular, proof of (1) and the module extension (2); Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular.

proof.text: For this fixed length, it suffices to prove the zero-relation assertion in each degree: $\sum_{|\alpha|=n}y^\alpha a_\alpha=0$ implies $a_\alpha\in JN$. Indeed, for the original sum $v\in J^{n+1}N$, step 1 gives $v=\sum_{|\alpha|=n}y^\alpha b_\alpha$ with all $b_\alpha\in JN$. Subtract to obtain the zero relation with coefficients $a_\alpha=n_\alpha-b_\alpha$. Once the zero-relation assertion is proved, addition of $b_\alpha$ puts the original $n_\alpha$ in $JN$. This reduction uses no induction hypothesis at length $s$.

source.place: Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular, proof of (1) and the module extension (2); Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular.

proof.text: Put $z=(y_1,\ldots,y_{s-1})$, $K=(y_1,\ldots,y_{s-1})$ and $t=y_s$. The prefix is weakly regular because its successive quotients and multiplications are unchanged. The last injectivity hypothesis says that $t$ acts injectively on $N/KN$. Consequently, for every $l\geq0$, $t^l a\in KN$ implies $a\in KN$: in the quotient, cancel $t$ successively $l$ times, with $l=0$ immediate. Also $KN\subseteq JN$ and $tN\subseteq JN$ by the descriptions of the generated ideals.

source.place: Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular, proof of (1) and the module extension (2); Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular.

proof.text:
Fix $n$. Prove by induction on $l\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$ that every relation
$$\sum_{e=0}^{l}t^e\sum_{|\beta|=n-e}z^\beta a_{\beta,e}=0$$
has every displayed coefficient in $JN$. The coefficients range over arbitrary elements of $N$ at each induction stage. For $l=0$, the prefix sum is zero and hence belongs to $K^{n+1}N$. Apply the outer induction hypothesis, in degree $n$, to the weakly regular prefix on the same module $N$. It puts all $a_{\beta,0}$ in $KN\subseteq JN$. This includes an empty prefix and degree zero.

source.place: Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular, proof of (1) and the module extension (2); Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular.

proof.text:
Let $l>0$ and assume the inner assertion at $l-1$. For $e<l$, each term $t^ez^\beta a_{\beta,e}$ belongs to $K^{n-e}N\subseteq K^{n-l+1}N$, since $|\beta|=n-e\geq n-l+1$. The displayed relation therefore gives
$$\sum_{|\beta|=n-l}z^\beta(t^l a_{\beta,l})\in K^{n-l+1}N.$$
The outer induction hypothesis in degree $n-l$ gives $t^la_{\beta,l}\in KN$. Applying the cancellation from step 4 yields $a_{\beta,l}\in KN$. No cancellation on $N$ itself or on $N/K^qN$ is being used.

source.place: Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular, proof of (1) and the module extension (2); Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular.

proof.text:
Write $a_{\beta,l}=\sum_{i=1}^{s-1}z_i u_{\beta,i}$ using step 1. For $|\gamma|=n-l+1$ let $b_\gamma=\sum_{\beta,i:\,\beta+\epsilon_i=\gamma}u_{\beta,i}$, where $\epsilon_i$ is the $i$th unit multi-index. Distributivity gives
$$\sum_{|\beta|=n-l}z^\beta a_{\beta,l}=\sum_{|\gamma|=n-l+1}z^\gamma b_\gamma.$$
Replace $a_{\gamma,l-1}$ by $a'_{\gamma,l-1}=a_{\gamma,l-1}+t b_\gamma$, and keep all coefficients at $e<l-1$ unchanged. Multiplication of the displayed identity by $t^l$ rewrites the original relation as a zero relation with upper exponent $l-1$. The inner induction puts all its coefficients in $JN$. Since $t b_\gamma\in JN$, subtraction puts the original $a_{\gamma,l-1}$ there too. Coefficients at smaller exponents are unchanged, and those at exponent $l$ already lie in $KN$. This proves the inner induction step, also for an empty prefix, where the sums over $i$ are zero.

source.place: Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular, proof of (1) and the module extension (2); Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular.

proof.text: Every degree-$n$ relation in the full list is exactly the relation in step 5 with $l=n$, by separating a multi-index $\alpha$ into its prefix $\beta$ and last exponent $e$. The inner induction therefore proves the zero-relation assertion. Step 3 proves the next-power criterion, completing the outer induction. When $N=0$ all the expansions and injectivity assertions remain valid; when $JN=N$ the conclusion is automatic. No finiteness, Noetherian, local, permutation, or nonvanishing assumption has been introduced.
